data: Sign in with passwords, connect a company identity provider, or let scripts use API keys. Describe your account rules to the Agent and reuse the application's authentication capabilities.
Choose an application database and connect external databases to use existing information in business pages.
Define roles, actions, and record scopes. Ask the Agent to apply the same rules to pages and server APIs.
Coordinate transitions, background work, waits, branches, and timeouts while keeping progress and history visible.
Connect Pro approval capabilities for conditional routes, joint reviews, added reviewers, and handovers.
Bring approvals, equipment collection and other personal work together with shared status filters and counts.

Managers handle leave requests, expenses and other applications every day. They want one place to see everything waiting for their attention without checking each business separately.
Add a My tasks page where each person sees only their own pending, completed and cancelled items, with a count for each.
Describe what should run, when it should run, and who should receive the result. Inspect schedules and execution history.
Send in-app messages or email when business events occur, with useful links and traceable delivery results.
Connect employee mailboxes to read, reply, organize messages, and relate correspondence to business records.
Upload, preview, and download files associated with records, with business permissions governing access.
Give the Agent an Office template and business requirements to implement document generation and download.
Add interface and server translations, configure the default language, and preserve individual language choices.
Adjust colors, typography, and density while preserving clear, usable light and dark appearances.
Connect page context, authorized business queries, and explicitly allowed actions to an assistant using your model service.
Organize business knowledge and connect retrieval so an assistant can answer with references to relevant documents.

auth.title: Authentication
auth.description: Sign in with passwords, connect a company identity provider, or let scripts use API keys. Describe your account rules to the Agent and reuse the application's authentication capabilities.

staff.label: Employee-only application
staff.text:
Northstar’s transport system is for company employees only.
Disable self-registration on both the sign-in page and the server.
Build an Employee accounts page for administrators, with name/email search and enabled/disabled filters.
Support creating, disabling, and enabling accounts, and revoking sessions separately.
Keep account creation separate from business permission assignment. Never grant administrator access by default.

password.label: Password requirements
password.text:
Require at least 12 characters when setting or resetting a password.
Show the requirement in account creation and password reset forms, with matching server-side validation.
Existing employees can continue signing in with their current passwords without an immediate password change.

recovery.label: Password recovery
recovery.text:
Add a forgot-password flow for Northstar employees using an email channel.
Let employees choose Forgot password? and enter their email.
Show the same submission message whether or not an account exists.
Use the email link to set a password of at least 12 characters and return to sign-in.
Reuse authentication’s expiring, single-use reset links.

sso.label: Company sign-in
sso.text:
Connect Northstar's existing corporate identity provider using OIDC.
Keep password sign-in and add a Corporate sign-in button to the branded page.
Employees visit the company identity provider and sign in with their company account.
Show consent explaining the basic identity and email requested by the transport application.
Return to the workspace after consent; canceling must not sign the employee into the application.
Allow account creation at first sign-in, identified by the provider's stable user identity.
Do not merge accounts by matching names or emails, or grant new accounts administrator access.
List the information the provider administrator must supply, the callback to register, and application configuration.

api.label: Script access
api.text:
Write a script to read Northstar transport orders.
Read the API key from NOCOBASE_API_KEY, never source code or logs.
Use the application's actual API documentation to select the order list endpoint and send the Key in the x-api-key header.
The example app is http://localhost:13200/main. GET /api/northstar returns workspace data; data.orders contains accessible orders.
Read orders, resolve customer names using data.customers, and output order number, customer, origin, destination, and status.
Handle API failures instead of treating them as an empty order list.
Explain how to configure the application address and run the script.

brand.label: Sign-in branding
brand.text:
Customize the existing transport application's sign-in page for Northstar Logistics.

Use a pale-blue truck and mountain-road illustration, a white page panel, and a pale blue-gray grid backdrop for readable text.
Show the company name and icon at the top. Place a welcome message and transport dispatch, delivery tracking, and team collaboration copy on the left.
Place a white sign-in form on the right, with dark text, white inputs, and a blue sign-in button.
Preserve username or email and password sign-in, password visibility, error feedback, and password recovery.
Disable public registration on both the page and the server while retaining the registration page and components for future use.
Use consistent branding on sign-in and password recovery pages, with Chinese and English copy.

protect.label: Pages and APIs
protect.text:
Add a public transport services page for Northstar without requiring registration or sign-in.
Use Northstar’s blue brand style to introduce its Yangtze River Delta network, regional transport, business delivery, and shipment coordination.
Show a contact email and an Employee orders entry. Signed-in employees can visit the public page too.
Its public reading API must not return internal orders or customer records.
Keep authentication and business permissions on the workspace, customer and order pages, and their APIs.
Direct anonymous visitors to sign-in when they open internal pages.

data-sources.title: Data sources
data-sources.description: Choose an application database and connect external databases to use existing information in business pages.

settlement.label: External settlement data
settlement.text:
Connect Northstar's existing settlement database as a read-only external data source without changing its tables.
Match records by customer number. Add Settlement information to customer details, showing the settlement cycle, credit limit, and settlement status, with the data source identified.
Keep reading customer contact details from the primary database. Read settlement information directly from the external database without importing it into the primary database.
Read connection credentials from server-side runtime configuration.

authorization.title: Authorization
authorization.description: Define roles, actions, and record scopes. Ask the Agent to apply the same rules to pages and server APIs.

permission-sets.label: Roles and assignments
permission-sets.text:
Create Northstar permission sets for account managers, dispatchers, and drivers.
Account managers enter customers and orders, create orders, and view or edit records they own.
Dispatchers enter the dispatch workspace, view transport orders, and assign drivers, but cannot maintain permissions.
Drivers view assigned tasks and accept, depart, and submit delivery evidence; they cannot change prices or reassign drivers.
Only authorized administrators maintain permission sets and assignments.
Provide job editing and assignments in Team access. Initially assign Alice and Bob as account managers, Emma as dispatcher, and Daniel as driver.

data-scopes.label: Record scopes
data-scopes.text:
Allow account managers to view and edit orders using the owner field linked to the current user.
Allow drivers to view and handle tasks using the assigned driver's employee account.
Allow dispatchers to view all orders needed for coordination, with assignment subject to current order state.
Provide per-action scope choices in Team access and enforce consistent rules on lists, details, and mutations.

default-access.label: Default access
default-access.text:
Keep account managers' owned-order viewing scope.
Add completed orders as a default viewing scope for everyone who already has View orders permission.
Let administrators save or remove the completed-order viewing rule in Access rules.
Add viewing only, not editing or transport actions on other people's orders.

sharing-rules.label: Sharing rules
sharing-rules.text:
Alice needs Bob to help follow up transport order NS-2026-001.
Bob already has order viewing permission; share this order's viewing scope with him.
Keep Alice as owner and preserve Bob's normal job and owned-record scope.
Do not grant editing, driver assignment, or approval through this sharing.
Let administrators select an employee and order in Access rules, save a view-only sharing rule, and remove it after collaboration ends.

restriction-rules.label: Restriction rules
restriction-rules.text:
Bob temporarily helps review transport fees and may view only orders with a transport fee of 2,000 CNY or less.
Add a fee limit to his View transport orders action, preserving his job and order ownership.
Apply it to his own orders, the completed-order baseline and shared orders.
Let administrators adjust or remove it in Access rules; explain that removing it may expand visible records.

inspector.label: Inspect permissions
inspector.text:
Provide permission inspection in Northstar Team access for authorized administrators only.
Select an employee and inspect pages, actions, record conditions, and sources from sets, assignments, default access, sharing, and restrictions.
Explain Bob's owned-order scope and temporary sharing of NS-2026-001 separately.
Do not present the inspection as an order count or let ordinary employees inspect other people's details.

workflow.title: Workflow
workflow.description: Coordinate transitions, background work, waits, branches, and timeouts while keeping progress and history visible.

definition-0.label: Business transitions
definition-0.text:
Add a workflow to Northstar orders: Awaiting dispatch → Awaiting acceptance → In transit → Delivered → Completed.
Assign a driver during dispatch. Accept and depart starts transport. Rejection requires a reason, returns to dispatch and clears the assignment.
Require delivery evidence to mark delivery, then confirm completion. Allow cancellation with a reason before departure.
Show only actions applicable to the current stage; ordinary editing must not change workflow stages directly.
Check stages and required inputs on the server and prevent concurrent actions from overwriting another person’s result.

execution-0.label: Background reports
execution-0.text:
Add a Northstar transport report page that exports current orders to CSV.
Queue the submitted report for background generation, then complete it automatically and provide a download.
Show the current stage, filename, exported order count and applicant/system processing history.
Retry generation failures according to policy and retain final failures for follow-up. Repeated execution must not create duplicate report files.
Retain progress and results after refresh, and allow only authorized people to export orders.

progress-0.label: Processing history
progress-0.text:
Show the current workflow stage and processing history in Northstar order details.
Record the actor, timestamp, action, previous and next stages, and rejection reason or delivery evidence.
Mark automatic actions as performed by the system.
Keep progress and history after refresh so the delivery process can be reviewed after completion.

approval.title: Approval
approval.description: Connect Pro approval capabilities for conditional routes, joint reviews, added reviewers, and handovers.

stages-0.label: Conditional approval
stages-0.text:
Add approval to Northstar special transport requests with cargo details, reasons, extra fees and attachments.
Fees of CNY 2,000 or less need operations approval; higher fees continue to finance afterwards.
Preview the route and reviewers before submission; show the current stage, offered actions and opinions in details.
Retain the approval decision without automatically paying fees.

joint-review-0.label: Joint and any-one review
joint-review-0.text:
Add joint review to Northstar special cargo requests. Both operations and finance leads must approve.
Reject immediately when either rejects, requiring a reason. After one approval, keep waiting for the other.
Use any-approval for routine dispatch: one on-duty supervisor’s approval is sufficient.
Show individual opinions and whom the request is still waiting for.

handover-0.label: Add or transfer reviewers
handover-0.text:
Allow adding a reviewer before the supervisor and transferring tasks in Northstar special transport review.
Added reviewers must be finance reviewers. The original supervisor continues afterwards.
Transfers must select the on-duty dispatcher and include a reason.
Retain original tasks, added or replacement reviewers, reasons and opinions.
Show the added-signer and handover paths with their reviewers in a flow diagram on request details.

requests-0.label: Return and withdraw
requests-0.text:
Allow Northstar supervisors to return requests with missing materials to applicants, with a reason.
Allow correction and resubmission, retain earlier opinions and determine reviewers again on review entry.
Allow applicants to withdraw before completion; reviewers cannot handle closed tasks.
Distinguish return, rejection and withdrawal, and show who should act next.
Show the return/correction/resubmission and rejection paths as a flow diagram in request details.

requests-1.label: Copy for information
requests-1.text:
Copy Northstar special transport requests to the responsible account manager.
Provide Copied to me and read confirmation. Recipients can view progress and opinions without deciding approval.

requests-2.label: Timeouts and claiming
requests-2.text:
Remind Northstar supervisors after one working day and escalate to their manager after two.
Allow eligible team members to claim tasks; release claims left unhandled past their deadline.
Show the current handler, deadline and assignment history.

scheduler.title: Scheduled tasks
scheduler.description: Describe what should run, when it should run, and who should receive the result. Inspect schedules and execution history.

reminder.label: Dispatch reminder
reminder.text:
Add a pending-dispatch reminder to the existing order application.
At 9:00 a.m. Beijing time on every weekday, find orders still awaiting dispatch and send one in-app notification with the count to the dispatch lead.
Open the pending-dispatch list when the notification is clicked. Send nothing when there are no pending orders.
Administrators can inspect the schedule and execution history under Automatic reminders, and pause or resume the reminder.

time.label: Change the schedule
time.text:
Run the pending-dispatch reminder at 10:00 a.m. Beijing time on weekdays instead.
Keep the existing order scope, recipients, and notification content.

report.label: Weekly report
report.text:
Generate last week's sales summary at 8:00 a.m. Beijing time every Monday and notify the sales lead.
Include revenue, order count, and regional totals. Administrators can inspect the task and execution history.

sync.label: Customer status sync
sync.text:
Synchronize customer status from the existing customer system every 10 minutes and update the matching records in this application.
Preserve other customer information. Let administrators inspect the schedule and execution history.

notification.title: Notifications
notification.description: Send in-app messages or email when business events occur, with useful links and traceable delivery results.

progress.label: Progress reminder
progress.text:
Add Send progress reminder to Northstar transport orders. Send the current order's progress to the acting user's message center through an in-app notification.
Include the order number in the title, and the origin, destination, and current status in the body.
Open the corresponding order detail without hard-coding a deployment prefix.
Send each version of an order to each recipient only once; repeated clicks must not create duplicate messages.
Preserve the current business status; sending a notification must not change transport progress.
Add Message center and an administrator-only Notification logs entry to the sidebar.
The message center shows only the current account's messages; logs show the business source, channel, status, and attempt count.

approval.label: Approval result
approval.text:
Notify only the applicant when a special transport request is approved or rejected.
Include the order number, request reason, and decision, and link to the request details.
Send nothing while approval is pending, and notify each result only once.
Keep the applicant's message center and let administrators inspect delivery logs.
A delivery failure must not undo the saved approval result.

email.label: Email channel
email.text:
Add email delivery alongside the approval-result in-app notification, using the configured email channel.
Read the applicant's email from their actual business account. Include the order number in the subject and explain the request and decision in the body.
Send only the in-app notification if the applicant has no email. Email failure must not affect the saved result or in-app notification.
Let administrators inspect delivery records per channel without exposing service credentials in pages or logs.

mail.title: Email
mail.description: Connect employee mailboxes to read, reply, organize messages, and relate correspondence to business records.

quick-start-0.label: Receive and reply
quick-start-0.text:
Add a mail center and a mailbox account management entry to the application. Users can connect their own mailboxes, select a mailbox, synchronize incoming messages, read messages and attachments, and reply.

When a sales representative receives a quotation request, they can reply from the mail center. Keep the original subject and conversation context, and address the reply to the original sender. Each user works with their own connected mailboxes.

usage-1.label: Email signatures
usage-1.text:
Prepare a Northstar Operations signature for the business mailbox,
including Northstar Logistics, Operations team, and transport coordination details.
Let employees manage signatures from Mailbox accounts and select them when composing.

usage-2.label: Progress email templates
usage-2.text:
Prepare a Transport progress update template with the order number in the subject
and customer name, origin, destination, transport status, and expected delivery in the body.
Provide the current order and customer when opening the composer from order details.
Employees can apply the template, edit the content, and select an existing signature.

usage-3.label: Customer correspondence
usage-3.text:
Add Correspondence to customer details.
Match the customer's contact email against senders, recipients, and copied recipients.
Only show messages accessible through the current employee's own connected mailboxes.
Select a message to read its body. Reply opens the mail composer with its reply relationship retained.
The employee reviews the content before sending. Provide Refresh mail and Load more.

usage-4.label: Order progress email
usage-4.text:
Add Compose progress email to transport order details.
Read the recipient from the customer contact and include the order number in the subject.
Populate the body with the customer, origin, destination, and transport status.
Employees review and edit before sending through their connected mailbox.
Allow existing templates and signatures; do not send automatically.

file.title: Files
file.description: Upload, preview, and download files associated with records, with business permissions governing access.

attachments.label: Order attachments
attachments.text:
Add attachments to existing Northstar Logistics transport orders.
Place an attachment area in order details. Allow multiple PDF, image, and DOCX files per order.
Show filenames and sizes, with preview, download, and remove actions.
Associate uploaded files with the current order when Save is clicked; keep them visible when the order is reopened.
People who can view the order can view and download attachments. Applicants and dispatchers can add or remove attachments.
Removing an attachment unlinks it from this order and preserves the file.

avatar.label: Employee avatars
avatar.text:
Add an avatar to each employee, with at most one image per employee.
Support uploading and replacing the avatar, and display it in employee lists and details.
Use the new image after replacement and keep it visible after refreshing.

templatePrint.title: Template printing
templatePrint.description: Give the Agent an Office template and business requirements to implement document generation and download.

docx.label: Generate a transport document
docx.text:
Add Generate transport document to Northstar transport orders.
Use my DOCX template to fill in the current order number, customer, origin, destination, cargo details, and transport status.
Preserve the template layout and repeating line items. Include the order number in the filename and provide DOCX download.
Read order data on the server under the current user's permissions. Do not accept arbitrary data scopes or template paths from the browser.
Check template fields and dependencies first, then implement generation and download and verify the document against a real order.

pdf.label: PDF download
pdf.text:
Add PDF download to the existing transport-document DOCX generation feature.
Check the PDF conversion service and fonts required by the rendering approach. If using the repository's Carbone example, configure LibreOffice in the application's runtime environment.
Keep DOCX download. Clearly report conversion failures or missing services; do not return a file disguised as a PDF.
Compare Chinese text, detail tables, pagination, and images against the original template.

i18n.title: Languages
i18n.description: Add interface and server translations, configure the default language, and preserve individual language choices.

add.label: Add a language
add.text: Add Spanish to the application. Translate both the interface and server messages, and add Spanish to the language menu.

default.label: Default language
default.text:
Set the application's default language to Simplified Chinese (zh-CN), keeping Chinese and English available.
Configure i18n.defaultLocale in config.yml so a browser without a saved preference initially displays Chinese.
Preserve existing users' saved language choices.
After the configuration takes effect, verify with a browser that has no saved preference and check that the page's lang attribute follows the actual language.

fallback.label: Complete translations
fallback.text:
Check the Spanish interface for text still displayed in Chinese or English.
Complete missing translations in the application's client and server. Override plugin text in application-owned translation files where needed.
Preserve the fallback order: current language, application default, then English. Do not translate business records such as customer names.
Run pnpm nocobase locales check and verify both interface and server messages.

theme.title: Themes
theme.description: Adjust colors, typography, and density while preserving clear, usable light and dark appearances.

adjust.label: Modify a theme
adjust.text: Update the Compact theme: change the primary color to blue and slightly increase border radii. Keep the current font, font sizes, and compact spacing.

brand.label: Add a brand theme
brand.text:
Add a Northstar Brand theme for Northstar Logistics, using deep blue as the primary color.
Base it on Compact, preserving the font, sizes, and information density while slightly increasing border radii.
Provide both light and dark colors with readable text and clear action buttons.
Keep the existing Comfortable and Compact themes, and provide Chinese and English theme names.

ai-employee.title: AI employees
ai-employee.description: Connect page context, authorized business queries, and explicitly allowed actions to an assistant using your model service.

index-0.label: Transport assistant
index-0.text:
Connect a Transport assistant to the Northstar application using my configured model service.
It explains orders, finds records awaiting dispatch and offers advice using transport procedures.
Connect order-reading actions within the current user's access scope. Start with queries; do not automatically change orders or send notifications.
Provide conversation entry points on order lists and details, with follow-up questions and links to returned orders.

page-context-0.label: Current order context
page-context-0.text:
Add a Transport assistant panel beside Northstar order details.
Associate the conversation with the current order and use authorized business actions to read its customer, route, cargo, status, owner and driver.
Summarize the order and explain the next action for its stage. Include the corresponding business entry point.
Update context when the order changes; do not reuse the previous order's information.
Use the existing blue theme and keep the order and conversation visible together.

business-data-0.label: Business queries
business-data-0.text:
Connect order queries to Northstar's Transport assistant.
Let employees ask for orders awaiting dispatch or filter by customer, stage or route.
Respect the current user's data access. Return the order number, customer, route and owner as cards that open order details.
Explain when there are no matching orders in the user's scope. Continue follow-up questions with the selected order's context.

ai-knowledge-base.title: AI knowledge base
ai-knowledge-base.description: Organize business knowledge and connect retrieval so an assistant can answer with references to relevant documents.

index-0.label: Connect a knowledge center
index-0.text:
Connect a knowledge center to Northstar for transport procedures, customer service material and driver handbooks.
Provide folders, articles, files, reading and search, with role-based access.
Let the Transport assistant answer from transport procedures and return document and passage links.
Connect the required model service, retrieval method and index while keeping sources clear in the employee interface.

answers-0.label: Source-based answers
answers-0.text:
Let Northstar's Transport assistant use the transport procedures space.
Retrieve relevant material before answering procedural questions. Include document and passage links.
Say when no supporting material was found; do not invent company rules.
Provide a conversation panel in the knowledge center with the original text visible beside the answer.
Respect the knowledge scopes available to the current user and assistant, including restricted finance material.

task-center.title: Task Center
task-center.description: Bring approvals, equipment collection and other personal work together with shared status filters and counts.

start.label: 1. Create an entry
start.text:
Managers handle leave requests, expenses and other applications every day. They want one place to see everything waiting for their attention without checking each business separately.
Add a My tasks page where each person sees only their own pending, completed and cancelled items, with a count for each.

approvals.label: 2. Connect approvals
approvals.text:
Include existing leave and expense requests in My tasks, showing their type and number to the person responsible for approval. Keep the approval rules unchanged.
After a transfer, only the new approver needs to handle the request. Withdrawn requests no longer need approval. Do not show the same work twice.

handling.label: 3. Handle work
handling.text:
I want to open a task, read the application and approve it, or confirm receipt when collecting equipment.
After handling, move the item to completed and update the remaining count. Only people allowed to handle it may act. Explain withdrawn items and stop further handling.

verification.label: 4. Verify results
verification.text:
Try the flow with two test accounts, Alex and Jordan: receive work, open details, handle it and check the remaining count.
Confirm neither can see or handle the other’s personal work, repeated clicks do not create duplicate work, and failed handling is not shown as complete. Tell me what was verified and give me a path to try myself.

ordinary.label: Equipment collection
ordinary.text:
When equipment is ready for collection, show the collection record in the assigned employee’s My tasks. Let them open it, review the equipment and confirm receipt.
Successful collection completes the item; an administrator withdrawing the issue cancels it. Do not show the same record twice, and keep it pending if collection fails.

dashboard.label: Dashboard badge
dashboard.text:
Show how many things I still need to handle on the home page. Clicking the number should open the matching task list.
Update the count and list after each item is handled. Show “No pending work” when there is none. After switching accounts, show only the new account’s work.

reassignment.label: Reassignment
reassignment.text:
An administrator needs to reassign equipment that Alex has not collected to Jordan. Alex should no longer need or be able to confirm receipt; Jordan should see and handle the collection record.
Keep completed collection history unchanged and avoid duplicate tasks if the reassignment is repeated.

history.label: Historical work
history.text:
There are already unfinished approvals and equipment collections in this application. Let the responsible people find these in the new My tasks page while retaining the original business records.
Do not miss new work, ask people to handle completed work again or show duplicate items. If preparation is interrupted, continue next time without starting over.

notifications.label: Reminders
notifications.text:
When equipment is ready, remind the assigned employee inside the application and let them open the collection record from the reminder.
Remind them only once per issue. Reading the reminder does not mean equipment has been collected; complete the task only after the employee confirms receipt successfully. A missing reminder must not prevent collection.
